reason: The counter move is a small, source-local scheduling test with low correctness risk, though its benefit may be small. Grouped stores and post-indexed stores could reduce address or store work, but the exact assembler forms need verification. Scratch layout and packing changes have more address and lifetime risk; packed B also adds work despite the current direct contiguous loads. The fallback-only tail proposal does not affect the timed n=512 path. Transpose fusion ranks last: the existing packed A data is reused across column panels, so fusing its transpose with compute appears to repeat transpose work for those panels and adds tile transfers inside the timed call. These are unverified proposals; prior noisy measurements do not establish causes.
